title: warp polydata
explanation:
### Description

Demonstrate warping PolyData using thin plate splines and grid transforms with different interpolation modes (cubic, linear, nearest) in an 8-viewport layout showing forward and inverse transforms.

**dataset → input → filter → visual_asset → renderer → infrastructure → output**

- [vtkActor](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkActor.html) — assigns the mapped geometry to the scene.
- [vtkDataSetMapper](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkDataSetMapper.html) — maps any dataset type to graphics primitives.
- [vtkGeneralTransform](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkGeneralTransform.html) — general transform.
- [vtkGridTransform](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkGridTransform.html) — grid transform.
- [vtkPoints](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkPoints.html) — stores 3D point coordinates.
- [vtkPolyDataNormals](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkPolyDataNormals.html) — computes surface normals for smooth shading.
- [vtkSphereSource](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkSphereSource.html) — generates a tessellated sphere.
- [vtkThinPlateSplineTransform](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkThinPlateSplineTransform.html) — thin plate spline transform.
- [vtkTransformPolyDataFilter](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkTransformPolyDataFilter.html) — transform poly data filter.
- [vtkTransformToGrid](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkTransformToGrid.html) — transform to grid.
- [vtkRenderWindow](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkRenderWindow.html) — displays the rendered scene in a window on screen.
- [vtkRenderWindowInteractor](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkRenderWindowInteractor.html) — captures mouse and keyboard events.
- [vtkRenderer](https://www.vtk.org/doc/nightly/html/classvtkRenderer.html) — assembles the scene and configures the camera.
- `Initialize()` and `Start()` launch the interactive visualization — `Initialize()` prepares the interactor and `Start()` begins the event loop.
